ai_summary.headline: Gaza has a large MPC line but only 8% of it is funded, while WFP cash is being cut.
ai_summary.narrative: Gaza's cash response rests on a large MPC line: $592.6m of the $4.06bn flash appeal (14.6%), with 1.15m people in Gaza targeted for NIS 1,250 per round, in two cycles of three rounds [s1]. Funding is the constraint. FTS shows $46.4m received for MPC, about 8% of the requirement, against 36% for the plan overall [s2]. The Cash Working Group reports transfers set to the MEB value and roughly 100,000 households reached in February [s4][s5]. Sectoral cash appears to be rationed instead: WFP said in July it would keep full transfers for the most vulnerable and reduce them for others [s6], and in October it cut cash for 75,000 families [s7]. With 1.4m people acutely food insecure [s11] and Gaza need put at 2.1m [s1], targeting likely amounts to triage within near-universal need. We found no source saying WFP's transfer falls short of the MEB. Cited surveys show 75 to 84% prefer unrestricted cash [s1].
barriers: MPC only 8% funded against 36% for the plan
WFP cash cut for 75,000 families; transfers reduced for less vulnerable households (Oct 2026)
Near-universal need forces triage; MEB-level transfers cannot reach everyone
Crossing closures and thin non-food supply complicate modality choices
opportunities: Established CWG with a harmonised MEB-aligned transfer value and shared deduplication
Cash-out commissions fell to 12% by Dec 2025; pooled fund runs MPC projects
